title: Local Light Pollution Analysis: A Multi-layer Evaluation Model

context_sources.name: VIIRS night-light imagery
context_sources.role: Night-light maps of Chengdu, Beijing, and Taishan

limitations: Equations 1 to 18 print as bare numbers; the expressions were stripped in extraction.
The notation table lost its symbols.
The summary uses the top 10 percent as the target while the body uses the top 15 percent.
The text says both three and four main indicators.
Table 8 shifts its rows, so the urban-planning grades are uncertain.
Table 10 for Latsia is scrambled and had to be read from column alignment.

tasks: Build a measurement model for light pollution risk at any location
Score a protected, a rural, a suburban, and an urban type of place
Propose three intervention strategies and grade their effects
Pick the best strategy for two real sites and promote one on a flyer

section_map.summary: Four pillars, four scores from 0.053 to 0.872, and two winning strategies.
Birds lose their way and people lose sleep.
Five numbered problems, the last a one-page flyer.
Night light only, fixed lamp power, and no geography.
Nine sub-indicators and entropy weights, light intensity heaviest at 18.99 percent.
Green infrastructure, energy, and urban planning, graded high, medium, or low.
The energy strategy cuts the risk by 4.80 to 11.65 percent.
Urban planning cuts the risk by 3.26 to 7.51 percent.
Energy moves the city's risk more than any other pillar.
Objective weights, but missing suburban and protected-land data.
Four actions for an urban community, from an audit to an education campaign.

contributions.summary: The weights are computed from the data by entropy, not chosen by the authors.
A cluster center stands for a whole type of place, so no single city has to be picked.
Each intervention is graded by the share of the gap to the ideal that it closes.
The same three strategies crown different winners in the two sites.

dependency_graph.handoff: The system model scores the four cluster centers.
The representative indicator vectors set the averages the strategies try to beat.

assumptions.summary: Nighttime luminosity stands for all lighting.
Lamps run at fixed power and cause fixed pollution.
Latitude, longitude, and altitude do not matter.
Building height is normally distributed with spread 0.2.
The best 15 percent of the data is an achievable target.

data_and_preprocessing.summary: Road impact coefficients borrowed from Yan and Tan.
Chengdu population and construction area, 2012 to 2022, from the municipal yearbook.
Eight indicators collected worldwide from the World Bank, the UN, and national offices.
Indicators normalized to the unit interval before clustering.
Tosca, Italy, and Latsia, Cyprus, chosen as the two application sites.

models.summary: Scores a place from four pillars and nine entropy-weighted indicators.
Finds a representative center for each of the four region types.
Grades three strategies by the share of the gap they close and picks a winner per site.

verification.summary: The ranking from protected land to urban matches common expectation.
Raising buildings, power, and roads raises the risk, and raising species lowers it.
The city is most sensitive to energy, agreeing with the strategy chosen for it.

results_trace.summary: Weights run from 5.52 percent for species density to 18.99 percent for light intensity.
Tosca falls from 0.7197 by 4.80 to 11.65 percent under the energy strategy.
Latsia falls from 0.2864 by 3.26 to 7.51 percent under urban planning.
The energy indicator produces the steepest change in the city's risk.

writing_logic.summary: State the purpose, then the pillars, then the scores, then the winning strategy.
Follow every assumption with its own justification.
Borrow a coefficient and credit its authors in the same sentence.
Show one city's growth before generalizing to the pillar.
Let the data set the weights and say that this removes personal judgment.
Define the grades before applying them.
Put the grade and its reason in the same row of the table.
State the expected direction of the test before running it.

language_observations.summary: A high indicator value is explained in physical terms, dense roads making dense light.
The weighting method is described by the judgment it avoids.
Each region type is interpreted in its own paragraph.
A site is chosen for being ordinary, and the text says why that helps.
The flyer keeps the strategy's four actions and ends with an invitation.

visualization_observations.summary: Figure 1 draws the study as a flowchart of four tasks.
Figure 2 shows the framework of the system model.
Figure 3 plots Chengdu's population, built area, and four VIIRS images.
Figure 4 draws the nine weights as a ring.
Figure 5 shows the cluster diagram for each region type.
Figure 6 plots the four regions across the four pillars.
Figure 7 shows VIIRS images around Beijing and the Taishan reserve.
Figure 8 compares the average and the target in all four regions.
Figure 9 shows Tosca before and after the energy strategy.
Figure 10 shows Latsia before and after urban planning.
Figure 11 plots the sensitivity of the risk to four indicators.

judge_relevance_hypotheses.summary: A judge rewards weights computed from the data rather than chosen by the authors.
A judge rewards reporting each strategy's effect as an interval instead of a point.
A judge penalizes a summary whose target quantile disagrees with the body.

weaknesses.summary: The summary says the top 10 percent and the body says the top 15 percent.
The pillar count is given as both three and four, and the notation symbols are lost.
The energy pillar is never given a formula.
The clustering quality measures are defined but never evaluated.
The impact grades are judgments with no reproducible rule.
The urban-planning impact table shifts its rows.
Suburban and protected-land data are missing, and politics and culture are omitted.
The conclusion speaks of four projects where the paper designed three.

independent_extensions.statement: Write the formula for the energy pillar and recompute the four scores with it.
independent_extensions.reason: Power and brightness are named but never combined, so the energy score cannot be checked.

independent_extensions.statement: Report the within-cluster sum of squares and the silhouette, and fix the target at one quantile.
independent_extensions.reason: The clustering is never shown to be good, and the target quantile changes between summary and body.

candidate_rule_impacts.impact: Supports letting a cluster center represent a type of place and checking the grouping with two quality measures.
Supports grading an intervention by the share of the gap to a data-derived target that it closes, and reporting the result as an interval.

unresolved_questions: How power consumption and light intensity combine into the energy pillar.
What within-cluster sum of squares and silhouette the clustering achieved.
Which quantile, 10 or 15 percent, is the intended target.
